text: A square matrix fails to be diagonalizable precisely when:
choices: it has at least one eigenvalue equal to zero
some eigenvalue has geometric multiplicity strictly less than its algebraic multiplicity
it has a pair of complex-conjugate eigenvalues
explanation: A matrix is defective exactly when, for some eigenvalue, the number of independent eigenvectors (geometric multiplicity) is less than the algebraic multiplicity, so nontrivial Jordan blocks appear. A zero eigenvalue only signals singularity, complex eigenvalues still permit diagonalization over C, and det equalling trace is coincidental.
